name: Hisao Nagata
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Hisao Nagata is the founder and chairman of Trial Holdings, a discount supermarket chain with interests in retail IT and developing AI systems. His son Hiroyuki is a director.

Nagata's father, Oumi, opened a thrift store called Asahiya in 1974 in Fukuoka, which Hisao took over in 1981. Three years later, he changed the name to Trial Company and also started a software developer focusing on retail.
Trial has developed technology to decrease labor costs and increase efficiency, including self-checkout shopping carts and AI-powered cameras to gather shopper behavior data and monitor inventory.
Trial has over 600 stores in Japan and posted $5.2 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended in June 2025.
In March 2024, Trial was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Growth bourse.
forbes_facts: The first Trial discount store opened in 1992.
Nagata has written books on retail AI and digitization, including one in 2022 titled 'How to Win the Retail Digital Transformation.'

name: Alberto Prada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Alberto Prada and his sisters, Miuccia Prada and Marina Prada, inherited a share of Prada, the handbag and fashion empire founded by their grandfather in 1913.
Neither Marina nor Alberto is involved in running the business, but each owns an estimated 12% stake in the company.
Miucca is a director of Prada and her husband Patrizio Bertelli is chairman. They each own a 28% stake.
Prada listed its shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Vicente Boluda Fos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Vicente Boluda Fos is the owner of Boluda Corporacion Maritima, the second-largest towage company in the world, based in Valencia, Spain.
The firm was founded in 1837 and expanded to tugboats in 1920 under Boluda Fos' grandfather. Boluda Fos took over in 1982 and expanded internationally.
Boluda Corporacion Maritima now owns more than 400 tugboats operating in 100 ports in 18 countries in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America.
The company also owns divisions in freight logistics, maritime terminals, mooring services and maritime insurance.
Boluda Fos also owns a stake in Bodegas Fos, a winery in the Rioja Alavesa region of Spain's Basque Country.
forbes_facts: Boluda Fos served a brief stint as president of Spanish soccer team Real Madrid from January to May 2009.

name: Rezwan Razack
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Rezwan Razack cofounded Bangalore real estate outfit Prestige Estates Projects with his brother Irfan, also a billionaire.
He's the joint managing director of Prestige.
Razack started out working in the family's textile and apparel business.
Today, Prestige's portfolio includes 300 completed projects across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality segments.
He works together with older brother Irfan and younger brother Noaman.
forbes_facts: Razack is a numismatist and an authority on Indian paper money with two books published on that subject.

name: Jenny Just
forbes_bio: Jenny Just started out as an options trader in Chicago, then cofounded options trading firm Peak6 Capital Management in 1997.
Just used her trading profits to start or buy about 15 companies through her investment firm, Peak6.
Her star investment: Apex Fintech Solutions, which handles the back-end trading and technology for fintechs such as SoFi, Ally, eToro and WeBull.
Apex Fintech Solutions canceled plans to go public via a SPAC merger in December 2021; the deal would have valued the company at $4.7 billion.
Peak6 also owns insurance company National Flood Services and e-sports franchise Evil Geniuses.

name: LeBron James
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2023)
forbes_bio: LeBron James is the first active NBA player to become a billionaire.
Born to a 16-year-old single mother, he lived with an assortment of family members, friends and neighbors, plus his youth football coach, before being drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003.
James has since gone on to earn upwards of $500 million in pretax salary from stints with the Cavaliers, the Miami Heat and his current team, the Los Angeles Lakers.
He has raked in more than $1 billion (pretax) off the court, according to Forbes estimates, from his business ventures and endorsement deals with brands including Nike.
Key to his billionaire status: James has been more than a pitchman, taking equity in brands he works with, including Beats by Dre.
His LeBron James Family Foundation opened its first elementary school in 2018 and has pledged to spend more than $40 million to send kids to college.
forbes_facts: James has publicly dreamed about one day owning an NBA team. As an investor in Fenway Sports Group, he already owns stakes in pro baseball, soccer and hockey teams.
In 2021, James sold a minority stake in his movie and TV production business, the SpringHill Company, to a handful of investors at a $725 million valuation.

name: Vera Rechulski Santo Domingo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Vera Rechulski Santo Domingo is the widow of Julio Mario Santo Domingo Jr. (d. 2009), who was the son of Colombian beer baron Julio Mario Santo Domingo.
She controls about 11% of the Santo Domingo family's Luxembourg-based holding company, through which she owns shares in Anheuser-Busch InBev.
Her two children, Tatiana Casiraghi and Julio Mario Santo Domingo III, own smaller stakes of about 5% each.
The family also owns a stake in Château Pétrus, a French wine estate near Bordeaux that produces some of the world's most expensive wines.
The family's public holdings also include stakes in Keurig Dr. Pepper and Kraft Heinz, as well as closely-held companies in Colombia, including movie theaters, supermarkets and gas distribution.

name: Douglas Rippel
forbes_bio: Douglas Ripple founded American First Finance, a company that offers lease-to-won and retail installment plans to customers, in 2013.
He sold the company to FirstCash in 2021 for $1.17 billion in cash and stock.
Rippel owns a 9% stake in FirstCash, an international operator of pawn stores
He served on First Cash? board of directors until stepping down in 2024.

name: Pavel Golubkov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2024)
forbes_bio: Pavel Golubkov owns 37% of home builder Samolet Group, which operates in Moscow and Saint Petersburg.
Golubkov founded Samolet with his partner and Mikhail Kenin in 2012. The pair went to university together.
The fast growing company went public on the Moscow Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Samolet is building residential complexes on land owned by such Russian billionaires as Roman Abramovich and Alexander Svetakov.
